task: EXL3 conversion baseline: Qwen3.5-2B-BF16 -> EXL3 4bpw on 1x R9700
hardware: 1x Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201), container rocm-exl3-r9700

input.model: Qwen3.5-2B-BF16 (Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration, hybrid linear+full attention, MTP1, vision tower)

notes: GPU utilization 100% on R9700 during quantization; single-device default (--devices 0).
Host user/sys totals include all threads and do not establish overlap or identify the bottleneck. Follow-up work adds direct capture/quantize/advance wall timers.
Baseline for the R9700 quantization-speedup work; no V620 comparison run yet (V620 pair busy serving the live TP2 server).

determinism_check.note: Wall time varied 17m27s vs 20m13s; the cause of this variation was not isolated. Output is bit-identical. SHA256 gate established for bit-preserving optimization work.

optimization_bit_identical.change: Ported quantize_tiles_optimized.cuh to RDNA (include swap over the bit-exact amdgcn codebook); enabled for K=4 only in quantize_rdna.hip; comp_units_rdna k4 returns the dense kernel. Commit 8d848c8.
optimization_bit_identical.why_bit_safe: K=4 dense path uses the same half2 arithmetic, the same rank-based NT-independent argmin tie order, and the same bit-exact codebook decode; K=2/3 (upstream initial-state fix) and K=6 (CUDA-only codebook LUT) stay on the plain kernel.

gates.gate1_kernel_bitwise: rocm_tools/qt_bitwise.py: identical hashes for every K x codebook, old .so vs new .so
gates.gate2_partial_qtensors: max_module 10: all 11 module qtensors SHA-identical to the baseline full run

optimization_bit_identical.negative_result: NT 512->1024 on the plain K=4 kernel (bit-safe by the rank tie order) measured ~3% slower and was reverted; this one geometry comparison does not establish the limiting resource.
optimization_bit_identical.remaining: The original estimate that capture/advance comprised ~2/3 of wall time was not directly measured. K=6 head/vision still use the plain kernel; its dense path needs a ROCm codebook-LUT port. Further work measures phase times and evaluates FP16-input/FP32-output Hessian products against BF16 and the original EXL3 model.
